title: Verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair to reduce LLM misconfiguration in vendor-diverse emulated NetOps tasks
research_question: Does an automated verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline significantly increase the oracle pass rate (reduce misconfiguration) relative to unconstrained LLM generation across vendor-diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks?
confirmatory_hypotheses: The verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases the oracle pass rate (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) by at least 30% relative (approx. ≥10 percentage-point absolute increase under typical baseline rates) compared to unconstrained LLM generation across the preregistered 200 tasks.
exploratory_questions: How do improvements vary by vendor (Cisco/Juniper/Arista), protocol (BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN), and task complexity (simple/complex)?
What is the distribution of repair iterations required and wall-clock latency under the repair policy?
How sensitive are results to validator strictness and repair-prompt phrasing?
benchmark_scope: Emulated vendor images and deterministic network simulator (containerized device images) limited to Cisco, Juniper, Arista emulations used in the testbed
Scope explicitly limited to emulation-based oracle pass/fail; no production-device claims
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute paired success-rate difference: guarded minus baseline)
secondary_estimands: Absolute and relative improvement in oracle pass rate by vendor and protocol
Distribution of repair iterations per successful repair
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: 200 paired tasks (each task executed under both conditions: baseline unconstrained generation and verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair). Protocol buckets (equal-sized): BGP 50, OSPF 50, ACL 50, VLAN 50. Within each protocol vendor allocation: Cisco 17, Juniper 17, Arista 16 per protocol. Complexity: within each protocol 25 simple, 25 complex. Total clusters: 3 vendors × 4 protocols × 2 complexities = 24. All 200 tasks are confirmatory paired units.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: detect relative improvement ≥30% (approx. ≥10 percentage-point absolute increase under plausible baselines). Two-sided alpha = 0.05; desired power ≥0.8. Baseline pass rate assumed plausibly 30%–60%; pre-execution paired_binary_analysis_v1 bootstrap simulation will report MDEs. Recommended scenario: 200 paired tasks (planned model calls ≈600 expected; adapter-constrained maximum_model_calls=400 given selected adapter limits; actual adapter-executed maximum is task_count*2=400). Sensitivity analyses: vary baseline pass rate across 30%/40%/50% and treat failed guarded calls as failures.
exclusion_rules: Pairs where one or both condition calls fail due to provider/infrastructure failure are excluded from the primary analysis (complete-pair primary policy) and logged in the execution manifest.
Pairs flagged as 'provider-drift-affected' (model identifier change mid-run) are excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis.
missingness_plan: Primary policy: require complete pairs (both condition calls returned an output); tasks where one or both calls failed due to provider/infrastructure failure are excluded from the primary analysis and logged. Secondary sensitivity analysis 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treats missing/failed guarded outcomes as failures (zero pass). All failed calls, API errors, and retries will be recorded with timestamps in the execution manifest.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis uses the registered analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 (estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Primary treatment of failed model calls: 'complete_pair_primary' (primary analysis uses only tasks where both condition calls completed); secondary sensitivity analysis 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treats missing/failed guarded outcomes as failures. Primary inferential method: paired-proportion via paired bootstrap (95% bootstrap CIs) implemented inside paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exploratory mixed-effects logistic regression (condition fixed effect, random intercepts for task/vendor) may be reported as exploratory. Subgroup analyses (vendor, protocol, complexity) are exploratory and corrected using Benjamini–Hochberg FDR.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test is the single paired estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). All subgroup analyses are exploratory and will be reported with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction.

stopping_rule: Execute all planned calls for the 200 paired tasks. If the frozen model identifier (provider/model id/API-version) changes mid-execution, mark affected pairs as 'provider-drift-affected', exclude those pairs from the primary analysis, and do not continue executing remaining planned pairs with a different model identifier; instead pause and record drift events. Otherwise, complete the full preregistered task list.
